verdict: ExxonMobil's profit more than doubled to $15.4 billion as surging refining margins lifted Energy Products earnings to $7.2 billion and sales rose 33% to $110.5 billion.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Sales and other operating revenue of $110.5B, up from $83.3B a year ago; total revenue including other income was $113.2B

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: Up from $1.76 a year ago; adjusted EPS was $4.23, excluding timing effects and identified items

kpis.label: Energy Products earnings
kpis.note: Refining and fuels earnings (GAAP), up from $1.8B a year ago on surging margins; $9.1B on an adjusted basis

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: Cash flow from operations was $25.7B; $9.4B was returned to shareholders in dividends and buybacks

segments.name: Upstream
segments.note: Oil and gas production — crude and gas sold to outside buyers. Most output goes to ExxonMobil's own refineries, so earnings are the better gauge: $7.1B, up from $5.7B a year ago.

segments.name: Energy Products
segments.note: Refining and fuels — gasoline, diesel and jet fuel sold worldwide, by far the largest sales line. Earnings jumped to $7.2B from $1.8B a year ago as refining margins surged.

segments.name: Chemical Products
segments.note: Basic chemicals and plastics that go into packaging, cars and everyday goods. Earnings were $735M, up from $515M a year ago.

segments.name: Specialty Products
segments.note: Higher-value products — lubricants, basestocks and specialty fluids. Earnings rose to $1.3B from $740M a year ago on higher basestock margins.

segments.name: Other
segments.note: Sales and other operating revenue in Corporate and Financing that is not part of a reportable segment — the small remainder so the segments add up to the company total.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative expenses
opex.note: Sales teams, offices and running the company.

opex.name: Depreciation and depletion
opex.note: The cost of wells, refineries and plants wearing out over time, including impairments.

opex.name: Other taxes and duties
opex.note: Taxes and duties on products and operations — separate from income tax.

opex.name: Exploration expenses
opex.note: Searching for new oil and gas, including dry holes.

opex.name: Non-service pension and postretirement benefit expense
opex.note: A credit this quarter: pension and retiree-benefit costs outside service cost reduced expenses by $20M.

follow100Note: The pension line is a $20M credit, so it adds $0.02 back for every $100 of sales. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Refining carried the quarter
takeaways.text: Energy Products earnings (GAAP) rose to $7.2B from $1.8B a year ago — $9.1B adjusted — as refining margins surged, year-to-date fuels utilization hit a record excluding Middle East impacts, and crude units at the U.S. Gulf Coast refineries ran at 100%.

takeaways.title: Profit more than doubled
takeaways.text: Net income rose to $15.4B from $7.5B a year ago on sales up 33% to $110.5B. Upstream earned $7.1B on production of 4,496 thousand barrels of oil-equivalent a day, and both Guyana and Kearl passed 1 billion barrels produced.

takeaways.title: Dividend up for a 44th year
takeaways.text: ExxonMobil declared a fourth-quarter dividend of $1.07 a share, payable December 10, 2026 — its 44th straight annual increase. It returned $9.4B to shareholders in the quarter ($4.3B of dividends and $5.1B of buybacks) and announced $20B of buybacks for 2027.

oneTimers: A $675M gain on the sale of assets in U.S. Upstream, partly offset by $226M of other identified items, for a net $449M gain included in GAAP earnings.

Unfavorable timing effects of $2,541M — mainly unsettled derivatives marked to end-of-quarter prices before the matching physical sales are booked — cut GAAP earnings. Excluding timing effects and identified items, adjusted earnings were $17,505M, or $4.23 a share.
otherDetail: Income from equity affiliates of $1,126M plus other income of $1,535M, less the $609M of net income attributable to noncontrolling interests — outside partners' shares of joint ventures — leaving $2,052M.
footerNote: Revenue is sales and other operating revenue; equity and other income are shown as other income in the flow.
